title: Geo-graceful eviction router and capacity-gating policy for multi-region routing
creator: Rishi Patel
description: Motivation: Our global customers are sensitive to p95/p99 latency and availability when regional outages or capacity pressure occur. Current steering rules do coarse region preference and blunt fallbacks which either cause capacity hotspots or abrupt thundering fallbacks. This ticket defines a geo-aware, capacity-gating request router that: (1) prefers low-latency regions while respecting per-region SLOs and capacity budgets, (2) gracefully evicts traffic to preserve global SLOs when a region degrades, (3) exposes circuit-breaker and token-shed signals to the Console, and (4) has an incremental rollout plan with safety knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Router implements latency-score + capacity-gate decision path: compute per-region score = alpha * normalized_latency + beta * (1 - normalized_utilization) + gamma * affinity_bonus

Per-region circuit breaker trips when error_rate > threshold OR sustained p99 > configured SLO breach window; trips expose 'region_out' signal and reduce routing weight to zero after soft-eviction phase
Soft-eviction supports fractional shedding (configurable 0-100%) with exponentially-backoff shrink/grow windows
Existing API behavior preserved for single-region customers; no API key migration required
Dashboard shows per-route per-region: p50/p95/p99, capacity_utilization, shed_rate, circuit_breaker_state; alerts for SLO burn and cross-region failover events
Canary rollout completes with no increase in global SLO breaches (defined as <0.5% added p99 latency breaches during canary).
design_notes: Decision: use asynchronous scoring at request admission to avoid adding tail latency; maintain compact per-region state cache updated by streaming metrics
Latency normalization: use rolling 5m p95 baseline per region; clip extremes to avoid noisy outliers

Capacity gating: per-region capacity budget expressed as tokens; tokens consumed proportionally to expected cost (tokens per 1k tokens generated). Token buckets refill rate derived from capacity curves published by Dedicated and Hosted teams

Circuit breaker logic: three states (Closed, SoftEvict, Open). SoftEvict reduces effective routing weight by configured fraction and serves as probation window before Open (full eviction). SoftEvict uses exponential backoff to avoid flip-flopping
Geo-pin semantics: user cookie/affinity header honored for retention window (default 15m). Affinity_bonus decays linearly with age to allow graceful migration away from starving regions
Fallback policy: region selection falls back to next-highest score that satisfies capacity gate or to explicitly tagged 'low-cost' model variants when capacity constrained

Tradeoffs: Aggressive eviction reduces local availability but preserves global SLOs; softer eviction increases cross-region load and inter-region egress costs. Tunables exposed in Console for operations teams.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local simulation harness using synthetic region traces (done)
Phase 1 (canary): 1% of cross-region traffic enabled for a small set of non-critical routes for 48h; manual verification of metrics and runbook drills
Phase 2 (ramped canary): 5% then 15% over 7 days with automated gates (no global SLO regression beyond target)
Phase 3 (regional pilot): enable for a single high-traffic region pair (e.g., us-west -> us-east fallback) with 24/7 on-call coverage
Phase 4 (global): full-environment rollout with default configs, then optimize per-tenant thresholds
Rollback: feature flag flip to disable new router; circuit-breaker fallback to previous region-weight table preserved for 30m during rollback
monitoring: New metrics: routing.decisions.count, routing.evictions.count, routing.soft_eviction_fraction, routing.circuit_breaker_state{region}, routing.capacity_tokens_used{region}
SLOs: route-level p95/p99 latency, route-level error_rate, cross-region failover latency delta
Alerts: region_capacity_utilization > 85% for 5m, sustained soft_evictions > 2% of traffic for 10m, any circuit_breaker Open event for a production region
Dashboard panels and annotation: show canary window, active circuit-breakers, and recent topology changes
runbook: Detection: console alert fires, paging the on-call with region and route context
Immediate mitigation: temporarily increase soft-eviction fraction toward 100% for impacted region to accelerate failover
If rollback needed: flip feature flag to previous router and monitor SLO for 30m. If rollback fails, escalate to infra/ops for capacity hunting
Post-incident: capture timeline, compute SLO impact, propose tuning changes to eviction thresholds and capacity budgets
